## Historical audit: S0348

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_113438548/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines; observations were not split across chunks.

**Goal versus evidence.** The assigned goal was to reconstruct an indoor photograph as editable SceneAct/Blender geometry, matching viewpoint, framing, objects and appearance—not to reproduce the photograph as a texture (line 1, `model_request`). The student interpreted the subject as a workshop tool display; that interpretation is not independent identification of the unseen reference.

| Stage | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Initial build | H emitted separate architecture, door, window, bench, display, vise, lower machinery and pipe assets, with named child parts. Wheel rims and spokes, vise jaws and pedestal were modeled separately. Color palettes represented cream, iron, glass and wood; no image textures are evident in the program. Parenting establishes a hierarchy, not verified physical connections or reference completeness (lines 3–4, `model_response`/`execute`). |
| First validation | Build and render completed successfully; the result included landmark projections and a saved image (lines 6, 8–9). The student subsequently reported the display as too small and a blank upper field and excessive floor (line 13). These are the student’s image assessments, not independently inspected images. |
| Camera exploration | H increased lens 43→82 and lowered camera target 1.90→1.65, while retaining much geometry (lines 13–14). In the second execution, small aim and lens trials produced directional projection tables; the revised frame top-left projection moved from (.346,.299) to (.206,.059), against the student’s estimated reference (.25,.06). Build and render succeeded (lines 16, 18–19). Projection agreement alone does not verify visibility or silhouette. |
| Final revision | H reported the frame about .05 image widths too far left, lower chuck too high, and window and bench too low. It changed horizontal camera aim, lowered the lower rail/chucks, raised window and bench, extended the pillar downward, split the vise pedestal to leave an opening, and darkened materials and warmed/reduced lighting (lines 23–24). A small aim trial shifted computed landmarks right; final chuck projection was (.428,.824) versus estimated (.42,.83), while the selected window-sill point projected outside the frame at x=1.26 (line 29). Step 3 built and rendered successfully and was selected (lines 26, 28–30). |

**Input and adoption.** The visible trace contains no separate teacher diagnosis or teacher-proposed patch. The task instructions requested inventories, projection checks and render comparisons; the next model requests actually supplied the preceding execution results and image paths (lines 1, 11, 21). H’s subsequent comparisons, trial projections and revisions show adoption of that workflow, not receipt of an unobserved teacher message. Its exploration was autonomous within the runner: three complete programs and two rounds of correction; the recorded model sessions show no direct tool calls (lines 2, 12, 22).

**Outcome and uncertainty.** This is a nonempty, technically successful build-and-render sequence, with the third build selected—not evidence of formal visual success or an algorithm failure. No final image review or independent score is visible. Multiple objects, color choices, hierarchy, camera and lights are evidenced in code; actual appearance, textures, occlusion, part contact, pose and final framing remain unverified here. The student’s camera-versus-local-error diagnoses are hypotheses, and the simultaneous final material and lighting changes prevent attributing any brightness effect to either alone.

**Transferable lesson:** numerical landmark trials can check camera-change direction while local edits preserve other geometry, but projections cannot replace full-image inspection. **Task-specific:** the chosen workshop inventory, offsets and lighting values depend on this reference and are not general rules.
